questions.ask: Could you tell me your year of birth?
Could you tell me the five-character customer code from your welcome letter?
Could you tell me your full date of birth?

intents.dispute: "This is not my debt" or "I never had this card".
intents.restructure: A request for a payment plan or lower repayments.
intents.vague: A vague period ("after payday") instead of an exact day.
intents.too_much: The customer says the full amount is too much.

lines.opening: Hello, this is a digital assistant calling for Halden Cards, and we record this call.
lines.robot: Yes, I am a digital assistant calling for Halden Cards.
lines.scam: I understand your caution. This is a genuine call from Halden Cards, and you can always call us back on our official number.
lines.purpose_before_verify: I can only discuss the reason for my call with {full_name}, after a few security questions.
lines.no_info: I'm sorry, I can't share that information.
lines.not_talk_once: I understand. This will only take a few minutes.
lines.tp_ask: When would be a good time to reach {full_name}?
lines.tp_ask_time: What time would suit best on that day?
lines.tp_outside_window: I'm sorry, we can only call back today or on the next two business days, between 9 am and 6 pm Monday to Friday, or between 9 am and 1 pm on Saturday. Could we call on {date} at {time}?
lines.tp_no_info: I'm sorry, I can only discuss the reason for my call with {full_name}.
lines.tp_booked: Thank you. We will call back on {date} at {time}.
lines.wrong_number: I'm sorry for the trouble. Thank you for letting me know.
lines.id_intro: Before we continue, I need to ask you three security questions.
lines.id_why: These questions protect you, so that we only speak with the right person.
lines.id_explain: The security questions protect you and your personal information.
lines.id_declined: I'm sorry, without the security questions I can't continue this call.
lines.id_repeat: Could you please give me that answer again?
lines.id_wrong: I'm sorry, that doesn't match our records.
lines.id_failed: I'm sorry, I can't confirm your identity on this call. Please call us on the number on your card.
lines.disclose_intro: Thank you, {salutation}. I'm calling about an overdue payment.
lines.product_line: On your {name}, {amount} is due, and the payment is {days} days overdue.
lines.ask_today: Could you pay the full amount today?
lines.ask_today_multi: Could you pay the full amount today?
lines.offer_floor_date: I understand. Could you pay {amount} on {date}?
lines.below_floor: I'm sorry, I can't record an amount below {floor}. Could you pay {floor}?
lines.date_past: I'm sorry, that date has already passed. Which day from today would work for you?
lines.not_business_day: That day is not a business day. Could you pay on {date} instead?
lines.after_deadline: I'm sorry, {date} is the latest date I can record. Could you pay by {date}?
lines.vague_ask: Which exact day would that be?
lines.ask_date_for_amount: On which day could you pay that?
lines.readback_intro: Let me read that back to you.
lines.clamped_note: For your {name}, the latest date I can take is {date}.
lines.recorded: Thank you, your payment promise is recorded.
lines.sms_line: A confirmation letter will follow by post.
lines.record_failed: I'm sorry, I could not record your payment promise because of a system problem.
lines.paid_line: Thank you for letting me know. Payments can take two business days to show.
lines.dispute_line: I understand. A colleague will look into this.
lines.hardship: I'm very sorry to hear that. I'd like to put you through to our care team, who can help.
lines.hardship_short: Shall I put you through now?
lines.restructure_line: I'll put you through to our payment plans team, who can help with that.
lines.human_ask_help: Is there anything I can help you with first?
lines.transfer: I'm transferring you now. Please hold.
lines.anything_else: Is there anything else I can help you with?
lines.promise_change: I'm sorry, I can't change that promise on this call.
lines.goodbye: Thank you for your time. Goodbye.
lines.callback_failed: I'm sorry, I could not book the callback.
lines.transfer_failed: I'm sorry, the transfer did not go through.
lines.confirm_again: Sorry, I did not catch that. Is that correct, yes or no?
lines.system_error: I'm sorry, our system is not responding right now.
lines.below_floor_final: I'm sorry, I can't record less than {amount}.
lines.recoveries_line: A colleague now handles your account, so I'll put you through to them.

assumptions: Amounts are spoken in euros: the API gives every amount in euro cents and the brief says to speak them in euros.
Workdays are Monday to Saturday (0-5), because the brief says Saturday is a full business day. The holidays are the three Halden dates the brief lists.
The brief does not define 'next <weekday>', so the default 'following_week' is used.

The brief's call variables are full_name and salutation, not first_name/last_name/title. They are declared in call_variables and used in the lines. confirm_ask uses the prescribed wording 'Am I speaking with {full_name}?'.
The brief says to tell the caller 'the call is recorded'. Per the spec rule this is phrased in active voice: 'we record this call'.

Callback days are 'today or either of the next two business days', mapped to ['today', 'within_business_days:2']. business_days_only is true because callback hours cover Monday to Saturday only. Sunday has no callbacks (windows '6': null) and Saturday's window is 09:00-13:00.
Callback max_asks stays at the default of 2: after a time outside the window, one valid time is proposed (rule 4), and refusing it closes as no_callback.
Identity: the API's 'one wrong answer is forgiven, the second locks the check' and the brief's rule 8 are counted over the whole check, so max_wrong = 2 in total.

The verify response maps 'correct' to verified and 'identity_passed' to all_verified. The API has no wrong-answers-left field ('wrong_answers' is a count so far) and no hint field, so 'left' and 'hint' are empty and hints is {}. The engine counts wrong answers itself.

A value in the wrong format is rejected with ok=false and is not counted as a wrong answer (API). The agent sends birth_year as 4 digits, customer_code as 5 capitals with no spaces, and birth_date as DD.MM.YYYY (%d.%m.%Y). Numeric dates are read day-month-year.
get_account returns one object under 'account', not an array. list_field is 'account', id_field 'product_id', type_field 'product_kind'.

Floor: the card uses floor_field statement_minimum_cents. The overdraft has no floor field and uses floor_pct 20 with floor_round up_unit (20% of the amount due, rounded up to a whole euro, not raised if already whole). floor_pct applies only to products without a floor_field. Credit and overdraft limits are never used.
amount_scale is 100 because get_account gives cents. promise_scale is null because create_promise also takes cents.
The middle band has a deadline per type (card: 8th business day after today; overdraft: 5th). The band default deadline is set to the card rule.
Early band deadline is end_of_next_week (last business day of next week, normally Saturday). Late band deadline is later_of(last business day of the month, 3rd business day after today).

Recoveries band (61 or more days): no deadline, no proposal, no promise. The spec has no recoveries event key and no band-level event, so this is modelled as bands_outside {'event': 'recoveries'} with an added events.recoveries (handed_over / recoveries, queue recoveries) and a recoveries_line. Bands 1-60 are listed explicitly; the brief gives no rule for values below 1, so these also fall to bands_outside.

Ladder: attempt 1 is the full amount on the 2nd business day after today, or the floor if the customer already said the full amount is too much (full_or_floor). Attempt 2 is the floor on the deadline. The early band uses only attempt 1.
'Full amount too much' before any attempt is handled as too_much_floor 'attempt_1': the single floor offer of rule 17 is attempt 1's floor on the 2nd business day, as rule 20 describes.
Rule 13 (Sunday or holiday gets the business day before, or after if that is before today) maps to deadline_adjust previous_business_day. Rule 14 makes refusing the deadline a flat refusal.
After a recorded promise, the brief only requires 'A confirmation letter will follow by post.' (sms_line). The default single 'anything else' turn is kept.

Hardship (rule 28): one sentence of sympathy, no persuasion, add_note vulnerable, transfer to care, close handed_over / vulnerable. transfer_support and hardship both use that outcome and note. hardship_declined does not mention the team again.

add_note in the API has no product id parameter (only customer_id, reason and optional free text). The engine requires the n_product slot to be mapped, so it is sent in the optional free-text field 'text'; reason maps to n_reason. Notes are written only for rules 24, 26, 27 and 28 (notes.enabled false; refusal has no note).
close_call reason is required for every outcome except promised and already_paid, so those two have reason ''.
The brief does not say whether a recorded promise can be changed, so promise_change says it cannot be changed on this call.
Rule 30 (ask once whether you can help before transferring to a person) maps to human.ask_first true. Saying twice they don't want to talk closes as no_commitment / declined (max_not_talk 2).
tp_outside_window proposes one valid callback time using {date} and {time}, per rule 4.
Only one product per call, so the multi settings keep their defaults and next_product is a generic line.
